name: Pelara Guava-Rosewater
manufacturer: Pelara Soft Co. (Corponation subsidiary — Vantage Consumer Group)
description: A lightly carbonated, pastel-pink soda built around real guava pulp extract blended with distilled rosewater and a touch of cane sugar. Marketed heavily toward Tier 3 consumers as an 'everyday luxury.'
flavor_profile: Bright, tropical guava sweetness layered with delicate rose florals, clean finish with gentle carbonation and no artificial aftertaste
slogan: A little beautiful. Every single day.
cultural_context: Pelara is aspirational Tier 2 — the bottle's frosted glass aesthetic is designed to look like something from Tier 3 shelves, and it works. It's the drink people bring to Tier 3 dinner parties when they can't afford wine. There's a running joke that Pelara's marketing team has a Tier 2 focus group they've never actually met in person.
story_hooks: Pelara's rosewater supplier — one of the last real rose-cultivating greenhouses in the Great Lakes corridor — has gone silent, and Vantage Consumer Group is sending someone to find out why before the next production run.
A street artist has been replacing Pelara's 'everyday luxury' ads with brutal parodies showing Tier 1 Shelf conditions — Pelara's PR team wants it stopped quietly, not through law enforcement.

The frosted glass bottles are being collected and resold as currency substitutes in a Shelf neighborhood where the local Φ exchange is controlled by a gang — Pelara is furious and confused about how to respond.
